title: Majestic Shield
transcript: Black's brilliant idea is pawn to G3, check, attacking [music] the king and forcing it to move. But there's a big problem. White is up an entire queen, >> [music] >> and three weak pawns are not going to be able to compensate for that. Or at least you would think that. But the white king only has two legal moves, either king to F1 or king to E1. And we can already notice that king to E1 would be a big mistake because it would allow a fork, protected by the G pawn. The F pawn would attack the queen and the king, winning the queen and the game. >> [music] >> But this should not bother white because he's just going to be able to move the king to F1. And now pushing this pawn would not be a check. White would simply win. And pushing the other pawn would not lead to a fork, so white would be safe. So is this it? Is doom scrolling simply going to win in this position? Well, not exactly. The player with the black pieces knows about Chess Shield, an app that blocks all distractions and only unlocks them once you've practiced chess. If you want to scroll, [music] you need to solve. And with the power of Chess Shield, black finds the majestic, brilliant, and incredible king to D5, [music] the only winning move, stepping away from the action and passing the move to white. But actually this move takes away the last few escape squares that the queen could have used, meaning that pretty much any square that the queen can go [music] to is under attack, leaving only two moves for white. Either king to E1 or queen to H1. But we already know that queen to E1 is going to lead to a fork. And now we can see that after queen to H1, there is going to be another fork, and black is going to win this game. You can download Chess Shield from the link in my bio and start improving your chess today.
